title: Experimental assessment of sustainable multi‐fuel strategies: Algal biodiesel, bioethanol, graphene oxide nanoparticles, and hydrogen fumigation in diesel engine applications
content:
Abstract

This study examines the combined effects of algal biodiesel (AB), bioethanol (BE), graphene oxide nanoparticles (GO), and hydrogen (H2) fumigation on a diesel engine. The test used a blend of algal biodiesel, 10% bioethanol, and 50 ppm nanoparticles, with H2 supplied at 3 and 6 LPM. Experiments covered 0%–100% engine load, with combustion analyzed from averaged pressure and heat-release rate (HRR) data. At full load, H2 induction at 3 and 6 LPM increased peak cylinder pressure by 11.04% and 15.95% and enhanced peak HRR by 33.33% and 47.61% compared to diesel. Correspondingly, brake thermal efficiency (BTE) improved by 4.89% and 12.97%, while brake specific energy consumption (BSEC) decreased by 34.82% and 51.15%. Emission results also indicated substantial reductions in CO by 55% and 75%, HC by 26.7% and 40%, and smoke opacity by 13.9% and 36.1% relative to diesel. However, oxides of nitrogen (NOx) emissions increased by 20.7% and 39% due to elevated in-cylinder temperatures resulting from the higher combustion reactivity and faster burning rate associated with H2. The study demonstrates a novel quaternary fuel approach, AB+BE+GO, with H2 fumigation, that significantly improves combustion efficiency and reduces carbonaceous emissions, offering a promising pathway to cleaner, more sustainable diesel engine operation.
